chunks: From him, from Sahl ibn al-Hasan, from Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-Dabbi, from Abu Muhammad al-Armani, from Abdullah ibn al-Hakam, from Isa ibn Attiya, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'I have vowed not to drink from the milk of my she-goat, nor to eat from her meat, so I sold her, and I have some of her offspring with me.' He said: 'Do not drink from her milk, nor eat from her meat, for they are from her.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a vow regarding the milk and meat of an animal after it has been sold?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the legal continuity of a vow (*yamin*) by ruling that the offspring and products of a vowed animal remain bound by the original restriction. This demonstrates the Shia jurisprudential principle that the essence (*dhat*) of the property extends to its natural derivatives, ensuring the vow's integrity is preserved even after the primary object is sold or separated. It highlights the precision with which the Imams interpreted the scope of verbal commitments in daily life.
